baselines.note: A naive net-rating baseline is computed in nba2/v2/strategy_lab.py and is not recomputed here; what is added in v3 is the paired test below, which compares the model with a *fitted-ratings-free* rule on the games they disagreed on.

margin_vs_total_model.withheld: the league-mean total is near-constant (sd 1.21) and its correlation with margin (-0.0034) is not a measurement of anything, so it is not published as one

correlations.reading: A spread/total correlation near zero is why a same-game parlay of a side and a total may be multiplied; a correlation far from zero is why it may not. The interval is published because at this n it is wide enough to matter.

holdout.reason: BLOCKED input 'odds': no market probability exists to measure a log-loss for

w_model_if_market_log_loss.note: L_market was NOT measured: no odds feed is connected. The two examples show what the weight would be for a market log-loss of 0.60 / 0.65, which is the usual range for a closing NBA line. They are illustrations, not inputs, and the site labels them that way.

future_only_edit.note: a fabricated game 30 days in the future changed no earlier forecast

leakage.rejected_test: delete-the-target-game. It fails on any correct implementation because removing a row also removes it from later dates' volatility estimates. Recorded here so the same wrong test is not proposed again.
leakage.rule: every prediction is computed from games with date strictly less than its own; appending undated-by-the-model future results is a no-op on every earlier forecast; and the deletion test that would otherwise be reported as a failure is explained above rather than used, because it confounds the date grid.

margin_shrink.reading: alpha=0.45 fitted on 110 games; held-out MAE 14.764 raw → 13.510 shrunk, against a tie guess at 14.500. The raw forecast is worse than guessing a tie; the shrunk forecast is better than it.

meta.source: data/raw/history/*.json + nba2/v3/official.py FINALS (official finals, one URL per row)

permutation.reading: the model's margin error is distinguishable from a tie guess (see the sign of observed_mae_gain: negative means WORSE than predicting a tie)

reliability.reading: The model's average distance from a coin flip is 0.277; reality's is 0.500. Every band at the extremes is over-confident: the lowest band claims 0.195 and delivers 0.384.

shrink.reading: Fitting the shrink factor on the first 110 games picks alpha=0.55; on the untouched 42 held-out games it moves log-loss from 0.7082 to 0.6398 (gain +0.0684).

skill.verdict: the second estimator is not separable from the first

total_direction.reading: Direction against a rolling mean over every scored game: 76/132 = 0.576 (z=+1.74, p=0.082) — not significant. On the subset where the forecast commits to at least a 3-point view: 65/106 = 0.613 (z=+2.33, p=0.020) — significant. The subset result is a threshold-selected subset of the same data, so it is reported as a subset and not as the headline; the whole-sample number is the one to trust, and the two together say the total's ordering signal is promising and unproven. Neither licenses a stake: a rolling mean is not a price.

calibration.free_fit_note: The unconstrained fit buys an RMSE of 1.0529 against the pinned 1.055 — a gain of 0.0022 — by claiming a home-win rate of 0.8312 against the measured 0.5294. That is the whole argument for pinning: the free parameter spends its freedom on a home rate no season has ever produced, and the RMSE gain is too small to distinguish from noise.
calibration.grid: σ searched 8.00→22.00 step 0.01 with h = σ·Φ⁻¹(p) pinned at p = the measured home-win rate; the free (σ,h) grid 6→26 / −6…+12 is reported only to show the identification problem

flags.what: The calibration shrink α=0.55 is a fitted parameter.
flags.why: It is fitted on one slice and scored on another, which makes the gain evidence rather than a derivation. A second season would test whether it is stable.

flags.what: Per-game travel understates multi-game road trips.
flags.why: The away figure is distance from the previous venue only. Accumulated trip distance is not carried, and a dash means unknown rather than zero.

flags.what: Quarter scores exist for the five 2026-11-14 finals only.

flags.what: The unconstrained HCA fit returns h=n/a.
flags.why: It is reported and not used: a free home term absorbs rating error and calls it home court. The pinned value is what the model publishes.

flags.what: The NBA CDN box-score JSON endpoint returned HTTP 500.
flags.why: No JSON API is available, so every number is scraped from a rendered page. That is slower and more fragile and it is why each capture names the exact URL.

flags.what: Two defects carried over from v2, untouched because they are outside this session's scope.

gates.name: Deterministic & reproducible
gates.why: every published number re-derives from committed inputs; the permutation test is seeded

gates.name: Leakage-free walk-forward
gates.value: same-date isolation, no in-sample term, future-only edit
gates.why: three direct tests of the leakage property; the naive deletion test is explained and rejected in backtest.leakage_audit

gates.name: Out-of-sample log-loss beats a coin
gates.value: raw A 0.7082 — LOSES to coin 0.6931; A×0.55 shrink 0.6398 — beats coin, on 42 held-out games
gates.why: The raw model does not beat a coin and is published saying so. Its probabilities are over-confident (reliability table: lowest band claims 0.195, delivers 0.384). Shrinking toward 0.5 by a factor fitted on the earlier dates does beat a coin out of sample. Both numbers are shown; neither is allowed to stand in for the other.

gates.name: Margin error beats a tie guess
gates.value: raw MAE 14.108 — worse than a tie (13.75) and worse than the league mean (13.658); ×0.45 shrunk held-out MAE 13.51 — better than both
gates.why: The model's margins are over-dispersed: it predicts a 13.4-pt spread where the truth spreads 16.8. Shrinking by a factor fitted on the earlier dates fixes the error but shrinking is not forecasting, and the shrunk number is not allowed to hide the raw one.

gates.why: two-sided p, Holm-adjusted across the family, and the verdict also requires the deviation to be in the direction the rule predicts

strategies.name: Two-estimator agreement side
strategies.settlement: side correct if the picked club's final score is higher. Push impossible: a moneyline has no line.
strategies.thesis: When two independent estimators agree on a side and the edge is not tiny, the pick is not an artefact of one model's scaling.
strategies.universe: every game in the results feed with ≥30 prior games (walk-forward)

strategies.name: Confident disagreement fade
strategies.settlement: side correct if the picked club wins the game.
strategies.signal: the OPPOSITE of sign(margin_b) when the two estimators disagree by ≥ 5 pts
strategies.thesis: A large disagreement means one model is out of its depth; the raw-margin estimator has scored better out-of-sample than the opponent-adjusted one in the v3 walk-forward, so the rule takes its side — and that direction is a finding, not an assumption, so it is fixed here before scoring.
strategies.threshold: |margin_a − margin_b| ≥ 5.0; pick the side of estimator A

strategies.name: Big-favourite moneyline (no line)
strategies.settlement: side correct if the picked club wins.
strategies.thesis: High-conviction projections are where a probabilistic model should be most accurate; if it is not, the probability scale is wrong.

strategies.name: Home-stand first leg parlay (2-leg, cross-game)
strategies.settlement: parlay wins if BOTH legs win. Priced with the measured cross-game correlation (assumed 0 across different games — a disclosed assumption, not a measurement) and printed beside the naive product.
strategies.signal: two independent games where each pick clears P ≥ 0.60 under estimator A
strategies.thesis: Cross-game legs are close to independent; the naive product is therefore close to right, and the print-both rule shows by how much.
strategies.threshold: both legs p ≥ 0.60; legs from different games
strategies.universe: pairs of games on the same date

strategies.name: Same-game side+total parlay
strategies.settlement: both legs win. Priced with the MEASURED margin/total rho from the backtest, and the naive product printed next to it.
strategies.signal: same game: side under A and an over/under read from the possession total
strategies.thesis: The brief asks for the measured rho beside the naive product rather than withholding the price. v3 measures r on 152 finals and publishes the interval.

strategies.name: Injury-rotation over (shape only)
strategies.settlement: requires a player prop line to settle; NO prop line exists, so this strategy is NOT MEASURABLE and is registered for completeness only.
strategies.signal: club has a top-8 minute earner OUT, so the replacement share is > 12%
strategies.thesis: Minutes redistribution is the mechanism by which an absence changes a total. The gate that stops it is a missing price, not a missing model.
strategies.threshold: replacement share ≥ 0.12 on the club's own box score
strategies.universe: clubs with a transcribed box score only (1 club-game in this capture)
